title: Sharing the road with driverless cars
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: raise your hand and move it from side to side as a greeting or to communicate with someone
(American English) crossing the road where it is not allowed or without taking care

sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好，这里是BBC英语教学的6分钟英语节目。

sentences.en: I'm Phil. And I'm Pippa. Here at 6 Minute English, we love discussing new tech.
sentences.zh: 我是Phil。我是Pippa。在6分钟英语节目中，我们喜欢讨论新技术。

sentences.en: One of the most controversial technologies of recent years is driverless cars, also known as self-driving cars, autonomous cars or robotaxis.
sentences.zh: 近年来最具争议的技术之一就是无人驾驶汽车，也被称为自动驾驶汽车、自主车辆或自动驾驶出租车。

sentences.en: Many people say they wouldn't feel safe in a car without a human driver, but there are concerns from other road users too – pedestrians, runners and cyclists.
sentences.zh: 许多人表示在没有人类司机的车里会感到不安全，但其他道路使用者——行人、跑步者和骑自行车的人——也有所顾虑。

sentences.en: How will driverless cars interact with them?
sentences.zh: 无人驾驶汽车将如何与他们互动？

sentences.en: It's a problem Professor Stephen Brewster, from Glasgow University, has been working on.
sentences.zh: 这是格拉斯哥大学的斯蒂芬·布鲁斯特教授一直在研究的问题。

sentences.en: He explained more to BBC World Service programme Tech Life.
sentences.zh: 他向BBC世界服务广播节目《科技生活》解释了更多内容。

sentences.en: If you're outside a vehicle right now, you can see the driver inside the vehicle, you can wave to them, they can see you, you can make eye contact.
sentences.zh: 如果你现在在车外，你可以看到车里的司机，你可以向他们挥手，他们可以看到你，你们可以进行眼神交流。

sentences.en: But when you come to an autonomous vehicle, there's no person in the driving seat, so how do you negotiate whether they're going to go, whether they're going to let you go?
sentences.zh: 但当你遇到一辆自动驾驶汽车时，驾驶座上没有人，那你该如何协商它们是否要行驶、是否要让你先过呢？

sentences.en: On my walk to work, I need to cross the road.
sentences.zh: 在我步行上班的路上，我需要过马路。

sentences.en: Usually, a driver makes eye contact with me.
sentences.zh: 通常，司机都会与我进行眼神交流。

sentences.en: They look directly into my eyes and then wave me across.
sentences.zh: 他们直视我的眼睛，然后挥手让我过去。

sentences.en: To wave means to raise your hand and move it from side to side.
sentences.zh: 挥手是指举起手并从一边晃动到另一边。

sentences.en: It's a gesture for saying hello, or a way of telling a person to do something.
sentences.zh: 这是一个打招呼的手势，或者是一种指示某人做某事的方式。

sentences.en: Luckily, Phil, you usually arrive safely at work and as yet there are no driverless cars in London.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，Phil，你通常能安全到达公司，而且目前伦敦还没有无人驾驶汽车。

sentences.en: But, Phil, how would you feel about crossing that road in front of a robotaxi?
sentences.zh: 但是，Phil，如果让你在自动驾驶出租车前面过马路，你会有什么感觉？

sentences.en: Well, maybe a little bit nervous. I might wait for it to go and go behind it or something.
sentences.zh: 嗯，可能有点紧张。我可能会等它开过去，然后从它后面走过去之类的。

sentences.en: Mmm... yeah, I get that. I think maybe as we get more used to these technologies, we'll get more used to how to deal with them and when to cross.
sentences.zh: 嗯……是的，我明白。我想随着我们越来越习惯这些技术，我们会更习惯如何应对它们以及何时过马路。

sentences.en: But in this episode, we investigate the tech helping driverless cars communicate on the roads.
sentences.zh: 但在本期节目中，我们将探讨帮助无人驾驶汽车在路上进行交流的技术。

sentences.en: We'll learn some useful new words and phrases, and as usual you'll find all the vocabulary on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 我们将学习一些有用的新词汇和短语，像往常一样，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到所有的词汇。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Pippa.
sentences.zh: 但首先，Pippa，我有一个问题要问你。

sentences.en: As you mentioned, we don't have self-driving cars here in London yet.
sentences.zh: 正如你所提到的，我们伦敦现在还没有自动驾驶汽车。

sentences.en: So, which was the first city to have fully driverless robotaxis on the streets?
sentences.zh: 那么，哪个城市是第一个在街道上拥有完全无人驾驶出租车的城市？

sentences.en: Was it: a) Philadelphia, b) Phoenix, or c) San Francisco?
sentences.zh: 是：a) 费城，b) 菲尼克斯，还是 c) 旧金山？

sentences.en: I'm going to say b) Phoenix because I think it's quite a car-friendly city.
sentences.zh: 我选 b) 菲尼克斯，因为我认为这是一座对汽车很友好的城市。

sentences.en: OK. Well, we will find out the answer, but at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的。嗯，我们将在节目结束时揭晓答案。

sentences.en: Because accidents are often caused by not seeing the oncoming danger, Professor Brewster wants to make driverless cars more visible.
sentences.zh: 由于事故往往是由看不到前方逼近的危险引起的，布鲁斯特教授希望让无人驾驶汽车更加显眼。

sentences.en: He discussed his work with BBC Tech Life's presenter Chris Vallance.
sentences.zh: 他与BBC《科技生活》节目的主持人克里斯·瓦伦斯讨论了他的工作。

sentences.en: What kind of signals worked in terms of alerting pedestrians and runners and cyclists to the intentions of the vehicle?
sentences.zh: 在提醒行人、跑步者和骑自行车的人注意车辆意图方面，什么样的信号有效？

sentences.en: We tested two things. We tested animations and fixed, coloured light rings.
sentences.zh: 我们测试了两种东西。我们测试了动画和固定的彩色光环。

sentences.en: The animations – they work well for pedestrians, but when it came to runners and cyclists, they have much less time to make their decisions, so if you do a quick glance at a vehicle, you don't really see the animation.
sentences.zh: 动画——它们对行人很有效，但对于跑步者和骑自行车的人来说，他们做出决定闪过的时间要少得多，所以如果你瞥一眼车辆，你其实根本看不到动画。

sentences.en: It's important to alert people to driverless cars.
sentences.zh: 让人们警惕无人驾驶汽车是很重要的。

sentences.en: To alert somebody means to warn them about a potential danger.
sentences.zh: 警惕某人意味着警告他们注意潜在的危险。

sentences.en: Some cars do this with animations – displays of moving images.
sentences.zh: 有些汽车通过动画来实现这一点——即移动图像的显示。

sentences.en: For example, a green man walking to signal it's safe to cross.
sentences.zh: 例如，一个绿色的步行小人来发出可以安全过马路的信号。

sentences.en: Animations alert pedestrians but are not suitable for runners and cyclists, who are travelling too fast to react.
sentences.zh: 动画可以提醒行人，但不适合移动太快而无法反应的跑步者和骑自行车的人。

sentences.en: They only have time for a glance. A glance at something means a quick look.
sentences.zh: 他们只有时间瞥一眼。瞥一眼某物意味着快速看一眼。

sentences.en: So, instead Stephen's team used coloured light rings, similar to traffic lights, to warn cyclists and runners.
sentences.zh: 因此，斯蒂芬的团队转而使用类似于红绿灯的彩色光环来警告骑自行车的人和跑步者。

sentences.en: Culture is another problem. The meaning of body language can change.
sentences.zh: 文化是另一个问题。肢体语言的含义可能会改变。

sentences.en: For example, hand waving can mean 'please proceed' in one culture, but 'thank you' in another.
sentences.zh: 例如，在一种文化中，挥手可能意味着“请通行”，但在另一种文化中可能意味着“谢谢”。

sentences.en: Ammar Al-Taie is a researcher at the Advanced Institute of Science and Technology in South Korea.
sentences.zh: 阿马尔·阿尔-塔伊是韩国科学技术高级研究院的研究员。

sentences.en: Here, Ammar tells BBC World Service's Tech Life why Korean culture is especially suited to self-driving cars.
sentences.zh: 在这里，阿马尔向BBC世界服务的《科技生活》节目讲述了为什么韩国文化特别适合自动驾驶汽车。

sentences.en: In South Korea, for example, jaywalking is illegal, whereas in the UK, you know, we tend to jaywalk a lot.
sentences.zh: 例如，在韩国，乱穿马路是违法的，而在英国，你知道的，我们往往经常乱穿马路。

sentences.en: Jaywalking is an American English word. It means crossing the road at a place where crossing is not allowed or without taking care.
sentences.zh: Jaywalking是一个美式英语单词。它的意思是走不允许通行的地方或不注意安全地过马路。

sentences.en: Unlike Britain, jaywalking is rare in South Korea, making the country safer for autonomous cars.
sentences.zh: 与英国不同，在韩国很少有人乱穿马路，这使得该国对自动驾驶汽车来说更加安全。

sentences.en: We've heard a lot about making driverless cars safer, and with plans to introduce them to London later this year, we'll soon see how safe they really are.
sentences.zh: 我们听到了很多关于让无人驾驶汽车更安全的讨论，随着计划今年晚些时候将它们引入伦敦，我们将很快看到它们到底有多安全。

sentences.en: Now, isn't it time to reveal the answer to your question, Phil?
sentences.zh: 现在，是时候揭晓你的问题的答案了吧，Phil？

sentences.en: I asked you which city was the first to have self-driving cars on the road, and you said it was Phoenix... and that is the correct answer.
sentences.zh: 我问你哪个城市是第一个让自动驾驶汽车上路的城市，你说的是菲尼克斯……这就是正确答案。

sentences.en: Phoenix, Arizona, was the first city in the world to have self-driving cars operating on public roads without a human safety driver, and that was in 2017.
sentences.zh: 亚利桑那州的菲尼克斯是世界上第一个在没有人类安全员的情况下在公共道路上运营自动驾驶汽车的城市，那是在2017年。

sentences.en: Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with eye contact – looking directly into someone's eyes.
sentences.zh: 让我们回顾一下我们学过的词汇，首先是眼神交流——直视某人的眼睛。

sentences.en: To wave at someone is a way of saying hi, by raising your hand and waving it from side to side.
sentences.zh: 向某人挥手是打招呼的一种方式，通过举起手并从一边晃动到另一边。

sentences.en: If you alert someone, you warn them of potential danger.
sentences.zh: 如果你提醒某人，你就是在警告他们潜在的危险。

sentences.en: An animation is a display made up of moving images.
sentences.zh: 动画是由移动图像组成的显示。

sentences.en: A glance is a quick, brief look at something.
sentences.zh: 瞥一眼是对某事物的快速、短暂的查看。

sentences.en: And finally, the American English term jaywalking means crossing the road where you're not supposed to.
sentences.zh: 最后，美式英语术语jaywalking意为在不该过马路的地方过马路。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up. If you'd like to hear more programmes about technology, you'll find plenty on our tech topic page, all on our website.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟又到了。如果你想听更多关于技术的节目，你会在我们的技术主题页面上找到很多，都在我们的网站上。

sentences.en: And there you'll also find a quiz and worksheet for this episode.
sentences.zh: 在那里你还会找到本期节目的测验和工作表。

sentences.en: Visit bbclearningenglish.com. We'll see you again soon, but for now it's goodbye.
sentences.zh: 访问 bbclearningenglish.com。我们很快就会再见，但现在要说再见了。

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见！
